context: Sortable stock dashboard table with 25 rows and 9 columns: ticker, company, sector badge (5 colors), price, 30d change, plus 4 embedded mini-chart types per row — area sparkline (30-day price), bar sparkline (7-day volume), win/loss strip (20-day returns), and bullet chart (performance vs target). Rows animate via translateY on sort.
first_impression: Dense but scannable — the tabular layout channels attention column-by-column rather than demanding simultaneous multi-view comparison, keeping cognitive load manageable despite 100 embedded mini-charts across 25 rows.
what_works: Five-color sector palette (Tol bright) stays well within perceptual limits and the badges are immediately legible. Alternating row stripes, sticky header with sort indicators, and consistent column alignment all reduce visual search effort across the table.
what_doesnt: The 30-day price sparklines share a single global y-axis domain across all 25 stocks, so a low-priced stock like CVX ($33) whose range is narrow relative to ABBV ($435) will render as a nearly flat line — local trends are invisible and the spark loses its core purpose. The win/loss strip cells are 4px wide with a 1px gap across 20 days, making individual day outcomes unresolvable at a glance; the strip reads as texture rather than a decodable sequence. Sort animation quality cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.
